verdicts.factCheck: Read on Ethereum at block 0x19426f6 through https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com. OptimismPortal.anchorStateRegistry() gives 0x23b2c629... (OP Mainnet), 0x27cf508e... (Unichain) and 0xee018baf... (Ink), and respectedGameType() on each returns 9. gameImpls(9) on the three DisputeGameFactories returns 0x19af533c..., whose version() is 0.8.0. gameArgs(9) begins with prestate 0x03e5a54835d39c1d83b198314473e1f111c3539c04f65c3e8a9b8ccebe3737c9 followed by VM 0xacc005dc..., whose version() is 1.10.1. Types.sol on develop defines SUPER_CANNON_KONA = 9 (line 81), PERMISSIONED_CANNON = 1 (line 57) and SUPER_PERMISSIONED = 5 (line 69). standard-prestates.toml lists 0x03e5a548...37c9 as cannon64-kona-interop for 1.9.0 and 1.9.0-rc.1 (lines 488-498). The Cargo.lock at tag kona-client/v1.9.0 pins revm 43.0.2, revm-interpreter 43.0.1, op-revm 20.0.0, ruint 1.20.0 and alloy-primitives 1.7.3. ruint v1.20.0 src/algorithms/mod.rs has target_arch x86_64 gates at lines 20, 149, 153, 159 and 176 with portable fallbacks. MIPS64Instructions.sol on develop implements dmultu as the full uint128 product (hi = res >> 64) and ddivu as exact unsigned quotient and remainder. The cycle 7 clearance in state/cleared.json does rest on the notice that no chain used kona as its respected proof at that time, so the finding is right that this ground has moved. No source contradicts the finding.
verdicts.codeCheck: The cited lines read as stated: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 mulmod(a, b, not(0)), :48 mulmod(a, b, denominator), src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:38 sar(8, signextend(2, tick)), src/libraries/BitMath.sol:16-22 the shl, lt, shr and byte lookup chain, src/libraries/TickMath.sol:104 div(not(0), price) when sgt(tick, 0), src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 the rounding mulmod. A different result in the proof program would not change any balance at the PoolManager on L2; it would only change which output root L1 accepts. The finding states this correctly and claims no loss path.
verdicts.corrections: The cited MIPS64Instructions.sol is the develop branch; the line numbers there need not match the source of the deployed 1.10.1 VM, though version() on chain is 1.10.1 as claimed. The link from the prestate hash to the kona-client/v1.9.0 tag rests on the registry entry, as the finding says. If an opcode divergence between the MIPS64 kona build and op-reth existed, both the triggering transaction and the challenge would be open to an ordinary account under permissionless type 9 games, and the effect would fall on L1 withdrawals rather than on PoolManager funds; with no divergence known, actor operator and severity info stand.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-663 part two: go1.25.9 GOARCH=wasm lowering of bits.Mul64, Add64, Sub64 and Div64 under holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 for the Arbitrum consensus replay.
clearedSpotChecks.note: intrinsics.go at go1.25.9 lists Mul64 for AMD64, ARM64, PPC64, S390X, MIPS64, RISCV64, Loong64 (line 1226), Add64 and Sub64 for the same set (1233, 1240) and Div64 for AMD64 only (1251), so the four are generic on wasm as stated. The item misses that Len64 and the TrailingZeros family are intrinsified on wasm (lines 978 and 902), and holiman/uint256 uses bits.LeadingZeros64 in division normalisation (uint256.go:529, mod.go:23) and bits.Len64 in BitLen and Sqrt (uint256.go:833-839, 1307). Wasm.rules line 331 lowers BitLen64 to 64 - i64.clz(x); the wasm spec gives clz(0) = 64, so the result equals Go's generic Len64 including at zero. The conclusion holds; the gap is that the transcription did not model this lowering, which rests on the wasm runtimes of the Arbitrum prover and JIT implementing i64.clz to spec.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Part one for World Chain: op-program 1.9.0 on Cannon MIPS64 with Mul64, Add64 and Sub64 intrinsified and Div64 and Len64 generic.
clearedSpotChecks.note: intrinsics.go lists MIPS64 for Mul64, Add64 and Sub64 and not for Div64 or Len64 (lines 978, 1222-1251), matching the item. dmultu and ddivu in MIPS64Instructions.sol compute the exact product and quotient. The respected game on World Chain is PERMISSIONED_CANNON (respectedGameType 1, read on chain), so only the operator's challenger plays the program and an ordinary account cannot use a divergence even if one existed.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Part three: Monad v0.16.6 and v0.16.7 do not change the compile decision or size bound against v0.16.5.
clearedSpotChecks.note: vm.cpp fetched at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 has the same md5 (cf49445c...) as the stored copies; x86.hpp is identical across the three; emitter.cpp differs only from v0.16.5 to v0.16.6. The release page lists v0.16.5, v0.16.6 and v0.16.7 and the RPC answers Monad/0.16.7. One caution: vm.cpp lines 166-172 compile immediately when the varcode cache is not warm, so a freshly started node takes the compiled path for the PoolManager regardless of the gas threshold. The claim that eth_call always uses the interpreter was not verified here, so eth_call results do not by themselves cover the compiled path.

leads.question: On a Monad node whose varcode cache is cold (vm.cpp lines 166-172 at v0.16.7), is the PoolManager compiled on its first execution, and does the RPC path for eth_call share that VM instance or use the interpreter only?
leads.why: If eth_call can reach compiled code on a cold node, the cycle 9 to 11 claim that eth_call tested only the interpreter needs correcting; if it cannot, block production on a restarted validator runs compiled code from the first PoolManager call.
